cues.en: Let's face it. Trains kinda suck in America.
cues.zh: 说实话，美国的火车真不怎么样。

cues.en: They're slow, expensive,
cues.zh: 它们又慢又贵，

cues.en: and just don't exist in many parts of the country. The simple reason for this is because The US is so sparsely populated. Aside from here, here, and here, cities just aren't close enough together to make train travel faster or cheaper than plane travel. When cities are within 200 to 300 miles of each other, it's often faster to take a train from downtown to down town rather than driving to an airport, checking in, going through security, flying, then driving downtown.
cues.zh: 而且在国家很多地方压根不存在。原因很简单：美国人口太稀疏了。除了这里、这里和这里，城市之间的距离都不够近，坐火车既不比坐飞机快，也不比坐飞机便宜。当两个城市相距 200 到 300 英里时，从市中心坐火车到市中心，往往比开车去机场、办理登机、过安检、飞行、再开车进城更快。

cues.en: However, as I mentioned, there definitely are regions in The US with cities this distance away from each other. So why do trains still suck? The United States has the geography to support trains in certain areas and yet a train from DC to New York costs at least $49 and takes three hours and twenty nine minutes, only thirty minutes less than driving. A train from Rennes to Paris, France, a very similar distance, costs €27,
cues.zh: 不过，正如我所说，美国确实有一些地区的城市之间就是这个距离。那为什么火车还是很糟糕？美国的地理条件明明可以支持某些区域的铁路，可从华盛顿到纽约的火车至少要 49 美元，耗时 3 小时 29 分钟，只比开车快 30 分钟。而法国雷恩到巴黎的火车，距离差不多，只要 27 欧元，

cues.en: the equivalent of $30, and takes only two hours and four minutes. The US does have one high speed train, the Acela Express, but it costs at least $120
cues.zh: 折合 30 美元，只需 2 小时 4 分钟。美国确实有一列高铁，Acela Express（阿西乐快线），但从华盛顿到纽约至少要 120 美元，

cues.en: for a ride from DC to New York and still takes two hours and fifty minutes. Turkey, Poland, and Uzbekistan all have trains that travel faster than America's fastest train. Alright, so understanding the whole issue requires a bit of background knowledge. Back in their heyday, railroads in America were amazing.
cues.zh: 而且还要 2 小时 50 分钟。土耳其、波兰和乌兹别克斯坦的火车都比美国最快的火车跑得快。好吧，要理解整个问题，需要一点背景知识。在全盛时期，美国的铁路曾经非常了不起。

cues.en: We built our first in 1826
cues.zh: 我们在1826年造出了第一条铁路

cues.en: and had a transcontinental line by 1869,
cues.zh: 到1869年就有了横贯大陆的线路，

cues.en: only nineteen years after California even became a state. Trains traveled almost everywhere and most historians agree that the development of railroads was an absolutely crucial catalyst to the American industrialization
cues.zh: 那时距加利福尼亚成为州才仅仅十九年。火车几乎能到达所有地方，大多数历史学家都认同，铁路的发展绝对是美国工业化进程的关键催化剂，

cues.en: period from 1843
They even prompted The US to create one of the world's first standardized time systems as discussed in an old video of mine which you can find here.
cues.zh: 铁路甚至促使美国建立了世界上最早的标准时间系统之一，我在一个老视频里讲过这个话题，你可以在这里找到。

cues.en: While passenger trains could sometimes be profitable, freight services were where the real money was. So most rail companies basically ran passenger services as a mobile advertisement for their freight services to the executives that would decide which company to ship goods on. Trains were, after all, the most glamorous and efficient way to travel.
cues.zh: 虽然客运列车有时也能盈利，但真正的钱在货运业务上。所以大多数铁路公司基本上把客运服务当作货运业务的移动广告，面向那些决定把货物交给哪家公司运输的高管们。毕竟，火车是最光鲜、最高效的出行方式。

cues.en: However, as cars became popular in the thirties and planes became popular in the fifties, there was little purpose anymore to set up passenger services as advertisement to executives who would be taking the more trendy car or plane instead. At this point, the few profitable passenger services only made money because of their contracts with the US Postal Service.
cues.zh: 然而，随着三十年代汽车流行、五十年代飞机流行，再设立客运服务来向高管做广告已经没什么意义了，因为那些高管会选择更时髦的汽车或飞机。此时，少数还能盈利的客运服务，赚钱全靠与美国邮政署的合同。

cues.en: Most trains would have one car that served as railroad post office, an office on wheels where workers would sort letters en route to the destination to save time. In the 1960s,
cues.zh: 大多数火车会有一节车厢用作铁路邮局，这是一个车轮上的办公室，工人在途中分拣信件以节省时间。到了1960年代，

cues.en: mail sorting was mechanized, trucks and planes began to transport letters, and railroad post offices were discontinued.
cues.zh: 邮件分拣实现了机械化，卡车和飞机开始运输信件，铁路邮局也随之停办。

cues.en: It became essentially impossible to make money with a passenger railroad. By the end of the nineteen sixties, the only thing keeping the few passenger routes alive was a legal obligation by the Interstate Commerce Commission for the train companies to keep running those routes. But then Amtrak came along. In 1970,
cues.zh: 想靠客运铁路赚钱基本上已经不可能了。到二十世纪六十年代末，仅存的几条客运线路能维持下去，唯一的原因是州际商业委员会有一项法律义务，要求铁路公司继续运营这些线路。但后来 Amtrak 出现了。1970 年，

cues.en: president Nixon signed into law the Rail Passenger Service Act, which formed the federally funded National Rail Company that promised to save and make great again passenger rail travel.
cues.zh: 尼克松总统签署了《铁路客运服务法》，依据该法成立了联邦资助的全国铁路公司，承诺挽救并重振客运铁路旅行。

cues.en: Except it didn't. In The United States, a nation of 319,000,000
cues.zh: 但事实并非如此。在美国，这个拥有 3.19 亿人口的国家

cues.en: people, Amtrak operates a mere 300 train journeys a day. While in France, a nation of 66,000,000
cues.zh: 人们出行靠铁路，而美国国家铁路客运公司（Amtrak）每天仅运营300趟列车。而在法国，这个拥有6600万人口的国家

cues.en: people, the Societe Nationale des Chemins de Ferre Francais, also known as SNCF,
cues.zh: 各位，法国国家铁路公司，也就是SNCF，

cues.en: operates 14,000
trips every single day, 800 of which are high speed. One common criticism of Amtrak is its unreliability.
cues.zh: ……趟列车，其中800趟是高速列车。人们对 Amtrak（美铁）的一个常见批评是它不准点、不可靠。

cues.en: On average, only 72%
cues.zh: 平均只有72%

cues.en: of Amtrak's trains arrive on time. The California Zephyr route from Chicago to San Francisco even arrived on time a paltry 31%
cues.zh: 的美铁列车能准点到达。从芝加哥开往旧金山的加州和风号（California Zephyr）线路，准点率更是只有可怜的 31%

cues.en: in June
cues.zh: 今年六月

cues.en: So what does Amtrak blame the delays on? Freight trains.
cues.zh: 那么Amtrak把延误归咎于什么？货运列车。

cues.en: You see, Amtrak only owns 730
cues.zh: 你看，Amtrak只拥有730

cues.en: miles of the 21,300
miles of track it operates on. On the California Zephyr route, Union Pacific owns about half the track and BNSF owns the other half. According to Amtrak,
cues.zh: 加州西风号线路上的轨道，联合太平洋拥有约一半，BNSF拥有另一半。据美铁称，

cues.en: only 1.4%
of all delays on this route were their fault. The other 98.6%
cues.zh: 这条线路上所有延误都是他们的错。另外98.6%

cues.en: were reportedly the fault of the rail companies who own the track. BNSF will naturally lend priority to their own trains on their tracks instead of Amtrak so Amtrak trains are often told to wait to let a freight train pass.
cues.zh: 据报道，这是拥有轨道的铁路公司的过错。BNSF自然会让自己轨道上的列车优先于Amtrak，所以Amtrak列车常被要求等待，让货运列车先通过。

cues.en: After all, a stalling Amtrak can go and use competing tracks so there's little incentive to give priority to passenger trains. Most rail operators in Europe don't have this problem. In France, for example, the national rail company owns all the track so priority can be given to passenger trains.
cues.zh: 说到底，晚点的 Amtrak 列车可以去用竞争对手的货运轨道，所以货运公司没什么动力给客运列车让路。欧洲大多数铁路运营商没有这个问题。比如在法国，国营铁路公司拥有全部轨道，因此可以优先保障客运列车。

cues.en: Also, only 8% of freight in Europe is moved by rail compared to 38%
cues.zh: 另外，欧洲只有 8% 的货物靠铁路运输，而美国是 38%

cues.en: in The United States so there are far fewer freight trains congesting the tracks. Since Amtrak is so young, they never got the opportunity to build their own tracks. The Northeast Corridor, which is absolutely perfectly shaped to have a high speed rail network with five major urban centers located on a straight line, built up its rail system in the eighteen hundreds and the railroad had such an impact that towns and people flocked to the area around it. For that reason, this area is incredibly densely populated and there truly is no open space between the cities. Consequently,
cues.zh: 所以欧洲拥堵轨道的货运列车少得多。由于 Amtrak 成立得很晚，他们从没机会修建自己的轨道。东北走廊的形状简直完美适合建高铁网络——五个大城市中心恰好位于一条直线上——但它的铁路系统建于十九世纪，铁路的影响力之大使得城镇和人口纷纷聚集到周边。因此，这一带人口极其稠密，城市之间真的没有任何空地。结果就是，

cues.en: it would be unbelievably
cues.zh: 要推平大片房屋、

cues.en: expensive to raze a bunch of houses and build a new straighter route of high speed tracks from DC to New York. Amtrak says it would cost an estimated $151,000,000,000
cues.zh: 从华盛顿特区到纽约修建一条更笔直的高铁新线路，成本会高得离谱。Amtrak 估计，

cues.en: to build tracks up to the spec of France's high speed rail network in the Northeast Corridor.
cues.zh: 在东北走廊修建达到法国高铁网络标准的轨道，需要大约 1510 亿美元。

cues.en: Since the Northeast Regional, the train running between DC, Baltimore, Philadelphia, New York, and Boston, is one of the few routes that makes money, there's little incentive for Amtrak to sink a lot of funds into upgrading the tracks. Additionally, American cities just aren't built like many European cities. With population densities averaging lower than 15,000 people per square mile, cities in The United States are far less walkable than their European counterparts,
cues.zh: 由于东北区域号（Northeast Regional）——这条往返于华盛顿、巴尔的摩、费城、纽约和波士顿之间的线路——是为数不多能盈利的线路之一，Amtrak 没什么动力投入大笔资金升级轨道。此外，美国城市的规划也和许多欧洲城市不一样。美国城市的人口密度平均低于每平方英里 15,000 人，远不如欧洲城市适合步行，

cues.en: which can have as many as 55,000
cues.zh: 而欧洲城市每平方英里的人口

cues.en: people per square mile. Due to their ancient roots, European cities naturally develop compact urban cores since for all but the rich, there was no option but to walk everywhere. Given that, it's much easier to walk to your destination from a train station in a European city than it is in an American city. It's believed that since most Americans have to take another form of transport to get to their destination after taking the train in America, they see the train as not that much more convenient than the plane where you also have to take another form of transport to get to your final destination. So what's the solution? How should America fix its rails? Well, unfortunately, we'll probably never get a big network of fancy high speed lines like in France or Germany. There are dozens of plans in The US to build high speed rail lines, however, few of them will likely come to fruition. There is a high speed rail line currently being built between Miami and Orlando by a private company called All Aboard Florida, however, with a top speed of 125
cues.zh: 可多达 55,000 人。由于历史悠久，欧洲城市自然形成了紧凑的城市核心，因为除了富人，过去所有人别无选择，只能步行出行。正因如此，在欧洲城市从火车站步行到目的地，比在美国城市容易得多。据认为，由于大多数美国人在坐火车后还得换其他交通工具才能到达目的地，他们觉得火车并不比飞机方便多少——毕竟坐飞机同样要在下机后换乘其他交通工具才能到终点。那么解决方案是什么？美国该如何修好它的铁路？遗憾的是，我们可能永远也看不到像法国或德国那样的大型高级高铁网络了。美国有几十个修建高铁线路的规划，但很少有能落地的。目前有一家名为 All Aboard Florida 的私营公司正在迈阿密和奥兰多之间修建高铁线路，不过其最高时速只有 125

cues.en: miles per hour, the service will only be slightly faster than driving due to speed restrictions on many parts of the route. The state of California is also building a high speed rail line between San Francisco and Anaheim with an estimated transit time of two hours and forty minutes, which would be less than half the driving time between the two cities. Despite construction already beginning, phase one of the project isn't estimated to be completed until 2029,
cues.zh: 英里每小时，由于线路许多路段有限速，这项服务只会比开车略快。加州也在修建旧金山到阿纳海姆的高速铁路，预计通行时间为2小时40分钟，不到两地驾车时间的一半。尽管已经开工，项目一期预计要到2029年才能完成，

cues.en: and public support is diminishing. Many have proposed that America shouldn't be concerned with building a flashy, high speed network. Amtrak's a $151,000,000,000
cues.zh: 而且公众支持正在减弱。许多人提出，美国不应专注于建设华而不实的高速网络。Amtrak有一项1510亿美元的

cues.en: proposal for a true high speed Northeast Corridor system divides down to $320,000,000
cues.zh: 提案，要打造真正的高速东北走廊系统，折算下来是3.2亿美元

cues.en: per mile or $60,000
cues.zh: 每英里，或6万美元

cues.en: per foot of high speed track. What would be far more efficient would be to upgrade current track to allow trains to operate at their top speeds. On the Northeast Regional route, trains reach a top speed of 125
cues.zh: 每英尺高速轨道。更高效的做法是升级现有轨道，让列车能以最高速度运行。在东北区域线上，列车最高时速可达125

cues.en: miles per hour briefly,
cues.zh: 英里每小时，但只持续很短时间，

cues.en: and if they operated at that speed for all of the DC to New York leg, the trip would take only slightly longer than two hours. Small improvements can cut minutes from the journey time, which can add up to hours. Unfortunately,
cues.zh: 如果从华盛顿到纽约的整段路程都以这一速度运行，行程只需略长于两小时。小幅改进就能从旅途中省下几分钟，累积起来可达数小时。不幸的是，

cues.en: Amtrak is stuck in a rut where they have no money to improve anything, which causes low ridership, which worsens the problem of no money. SNCF in France is so great because taxpayers pay for about half of the operating cost of every journey, while Amtrak is designed to be a for profit yet government subsidized corporation.
cues.zh: Amtrak陷入恶性循环：没钱改善任何东西，导致乘客量低，而乘客量低又加剧了没钱的问题。法国SNCF之所以出色，是因为纳税人承担了每趟行程约一半的运营成本，而Amtrak被设计成一家营利性但接受政府补贴的公司。

cues.en: Right now, Amtrak is kinda like the neglected little brother in The US transit family who doesn't get any money, and until that changes, we're still gonna have our slow,
cues.zh: 眼下，Amtrak 有点像美国交通大家庭里被忽视的小弟，拿不到什么钱；除非这一点改变，否则我们仍会拥有又慢、

cues.en: expensive trains.
cues.zh: 又贵的列车。
